records.quote: The Transformer model relies solely on attention networks, with additional sinusoid-style position encoding added to input embedding.

records.claim: The Transformer network consists of a stack of 6 encoder layers and 6 decoder layers.
records.quote: The Transformer network consists of a stack of 6 encoder layers and 6 decoder layers.

records.quote: To stabilize optimization, Transformer uses residual connection and layer normalization in each sub-layer.

records.quote: Researchers [ 25 , 26 , 27 , 28 ] have found that models with right-to-left (R2L) factorization are complementary to L2R models.

records.claim: Non-autoregressive NMTs avoid the auto-regressive property and produce outputs in parallel, allowing much lower latency during inference.
records.quote: In addition to auto-regressive approaches where each output word on previously generated outputs, non-autoregressive NMTs [ 29 ] avoids this auto-regressive property and produces outputs in parallel, allowing much lower latency during inference.

records.quote: The statistical results show that, in Chinese-English translation, L2R performs better in the first 4 tokens while R2L translates better in the last 4 tokens.

claims.claim: Bidirectional decoding based methods can be mainly fall into four categories: agreement between L2R and R2L, rescore with bidirectional decoding, asynchronous bidirectional decoding, and synchronous bidirectional decoding.

records.quote: Bidirectional decoding based methods can be mainly fall into four categories [ 33 ] : (1) agreement between L2R and R2L [ 25 , 34 , 35 ] , (2) rescore with bidirectional decoding [ 25 , 36 ] , (3) asynchronous bidirectional decoding [ 27 , 37 ] , and (4) synchronous bidirectional decoding [ 28 , 38 , 39 ] .

records.quote: Extensive experiments demonstrate that this method can improve not only the accuracy of translation but also decoding efficiency.

records.quote: To reduce the latency during inference, Gu et al. [29] first proposed the non-autoregressive NMT (NAT) to generate the target words in parallel.

records.quote: To take advantage of both autoregressive NMT and non-autoregressive NMT, Wang et al. [47] designed a semi-autoregressive Transformer (SAT) model.

records.claim: Akoury et al. moved a further step to propose SynST, which autoregressively predicts a chunked parse tree and then generates all words in one shot.
records.quote: Akoury et al. [53] moved a further step to propose a syntactically supervised Transformer (SynST), which first autoregressively predicts a chunked parse tree and then generates all words in one shot conditioned on the predicted parse.

records.claim: Guo et al. proposed using a phrase table to convert source words to target words to address the issue of ignoring semantic differences between source and target in NAT.

records.claim: A continual learner is an autonomous agent learning over an endless stream of tasks with desiderata including online learning, task agnosticism, incremental learning without fixed training sets, retention of previous abilities to minimize catastrophic forgetting, and efficient adaptation to changes.
records.quote: A continual learner can be seen as an autonomous agent learning over an endless stream of tasks, which has the following desiderata in the context of learning: 1) it can learn online, 2) it learns behaviors or skills while solving presented tasks, 3) learning is task agnostic, 4) it learns incrementally with no fixed training set, 5) it learns behaviors that can be built upon later, 6) it retains previously learned abilities i.e. it minimizes catastrophic forgetting and interference, and 7) it adapts efficiently to changes experienced over time and recovers quickly.

records.subject: Distillation Based

claims.claim: Leveraging knowledge distillation from past tasks is a common way to encourage retention of knowledge and prevent catastrophic forgetting.
Distillation can be used to augment experiences for training a network by providing a new auxiliary target for the network being trained to match.

In a continual learning context, distillation is a popular strategy for implementing conservative updates so that the agent’s learning has stability in preserving important knowledge of past tasks whenever possible.
The distillation approach ultimately learns a separate model for each task, which could help address issues of Pareto optimality when an agent must learn conflicting tasks.
The distillation approach results in the need for a knowledge compression strategy to scale to true many task learning settings.

records.quote: Another common way to encourage retention of knowledge from past tasks is by leveraging knowledge distillation ( Buciluǎ et al., 2006 ; Hinton et al., 2015 ) from past tasks when learning a new task to prevent catastrophic forgetting as in ( Rusu et al., 2015 ; Li and Hoiem, 2016 ; Riemer et al., 2016 ; Espeholt et al., 2018 ; Schwarz et al., 2018 ; Berseth et al., 2018 ; Kaplanis et al., 2019 ; Traoré et al., 2019 ; Tirumala et al., 2019 ; Igl et al., 2021 ; Lan et al., 2022 ; Zhang et al., 2022 ) . Knowledge distillation refers to the process of using one neural network as a target or soft target for another. Distillation can be used to augment experiences for training a network by providing a new auxiliary target for the network being trained to match. In the context of RL, this target could refer to either a policy or value function. In a continual learning context, distillation is a popular strategy for implementing conservative updates so that the agent’s learning has stability in preserving important knowledge of past tasks whenever possible. An additional benefit of this distillation approach is that it ultimately learns a separate model for each task, which could help address issues of Pareto optimality when an agent must learn conflicting tasks. On the other hand, this results in the need for a knowledge compression strategy for distillation approaches to scale to true many task learning settings.

claims.claim: The first set of metrics evaluates overall quality, including validity, uniqueness, novelty, reconstruction, internal diversity, NLL, and structural statistics like SNN or fragment/scaffold similarity.

records.quote: the molecular graph generators adopt two different sets of metrics where the first set contains those evaluating the overall quality of generated samples, including validity , uniqueness , novelty , reconstruction , internal diversity , negative log-likelihood (NLL) , and some structural statistics like nearest neighbor similarity (SNN) or fragment/scaffold similarity . The second set, on the other hand, contains metrics assessing special chemical properties of the molecules, namely, synthetic accessibility score (SA score) [ 151 ] , drug-likeness score (QED) [ 152 ] , molecular weight (MW) , log partition coefficient (logP) , penalized logP , and topological polar surface area (TPSA) .

records.subject: phased array antenna design

claims.claim: Phased array antenna designs use phase shifted small gain antennas to create a steerable high gain beam without mechanical rotation.
This design is important in millimeter wave communication systems due to penetration loss and reliance on Line of Sight propagation requiring constant beam re-alignment.

records.quote: The phased array antenna design is an antenna array design in which densely packed small gain antenna’s are phase shifted by a separate analog or digital phase shift module to create an overall high gain beam that can be steered without mechanically rotating the antenna’s [ 163 ] . This antenna array design is very important in millimeter wave communication systems since, due to experiencing more penentration loss than centimeter wave communication systems and solely relying on Line of Sight (LOS) propagation, transmitter and receiver beams constantly have to be re-aligned [ 10 ] .

records.subject: Active Imaging

claims.claim: Mechanical scanning includes line array scanning, plane scanning, and moving a small radar system in two directions on a virtual plane.
Free space scanning uses the forward motion of a radar connected to a moving device, such as a drone or planetary lander, to construct images.

records.quote: The literature covers three types of mechanical scanning. In line array scanning, a 1-dimensional array of antenna’s on a straight line scan in a single direction back and forth (i.e., up/down or right/left) [ 141 , 149 , 151 , 152 ] . In plane scanning, antennas arranged into a 2-dimensional plane scan the target from different distances by moving perpendicular to the plane [ 156 ] . Some papers employ scanning a target by moving a small radar system in two directions on a virtual plane [ 175 , 142 , 178 , 154 , 179 ] . In the so called free space scanning method, the forward motion of a radar connected to a moving device, such as a drone or planetary lander, is used to construct images.

records.subject: Spatial contextual feature generation

claims.claim: Spatial contextual features can be generated based on spatial relationships with other locations or objects, such as distance or direction, touching, lying within or overlapping with another object.
Spatial contextual features have long been used in classifying raster data (e.g., earth observation imagery) to reduce salt-and-pepper noise.
claims.claims_about: Spatial contextual features on raster data

claims.claim: Information from different sources can be fused into the same spatial framework, providing important spatial contexts for learning samples.
claims.claims_about: Spatial contextual features from multi-source data fusion

records.quote: Spatial relationship features : Spatial contextual features can be generated based on spatial relationships with other locations or objects, such as distance or direction, touching, lying within or overlapping with another object. Spatial relationship features can be readily used in rule-based or decision tree-based models. Examples of techniques include spatiotemporal probability tree model to classify meteorological data on storms [ 37 , 38 ] , multi-relational spatial classification [ 39 ] , prediction based on spatial association rules [ 40 ] . Spatial contextual features on raster data : Spatial contextual features have long been used in classifying raster data (e.g., earth observation imagery) to reduce salt-and-pepper noise [ 41 ] . Specific methods include neighborhood window filters (e.g., median filter [ 42 ] , weighted median filter [ 43 ] , adaptive median filter [ 44 ] , decision-based filter [ 42 , 45 ] , etc.), spatial contextual variables and textures [ 46 ] , neighborhood spatial autocorrelation statistics [ 24 , 47 ] , morphological profiling [ 48 ] , and object-based image analysis (e.g., mean, variance, texture of object segments) [ 49 ] . Sometimes, these methods are used in the post-processing step [ 50 ] . Spatial contextual features from multi-source data fusion : One unique property of spatial data is that information from different sources can be fused into the same spatial framework, providing important spatial contexts for learning samples. For example, when predicting a fine-grained air quality map for an entire city, we can generate contextual features by fusing air quality records at ground stations, weather information, road network and traffic data, as well as POIs [ 51 ] . When predicting human behaviors from location history, auxiliary data from geosocial media can provide important semantic annotations [ 52 , 53 ] . Generating contextual features through data fusion can have its own challenges (e.g., multi-modality, sparsity, noise). Various techniques have been explored such as coupled matrix factorization, and context-aware tensor decomposition with manifold [ 54 ] .

records.subject: Active learning

claims.claim: Addresses the challenge of limited ground truth by manually labeling a carefully selected subset of unlabeled samples.
Strategies include selecting samples with highest uncertainty, most committee disagreement, highest expected model change, or best expected error reduction.

records.quote: Active learning [ 114 , 115 ] addresses the challenge of limited ground truth by manually labeling a carefully selected subset of unlabeled samples. The main question is how to select the subset of unlabeled samples that can enhance prediction performance the most and with the minimum labeling costs. There are several strategies to do this, including selecting samples with the highest uncertainty, samples on which a committee of models disagree the most, samples that have the highest expected model change, or samples with the best expected error reduction.

claims.conditions: according to the input source types

claims.claim: Methods using monocular RGB images and videos are further divided into single-view single-person, single-view multi-person, and multi-view methods.

records.quote: HPE is divided into two main categories: 2D HPE (§ 2 ) and 3D HPE (§ 3 ). Fig. 1 shows the taxonomy of deep learning methods for HPE. According to the number of people, 2D HPE methods are categorized into single-person and multi-person settings. For single-person methods (§ 2.1 ), there are two categories: regression methods and heatmap-based methods. For multi-person methods (§ 2.2 ), there are also two types of methods: top-down methods and bottom-up methods. 3D HPE methods are classified according to the input source types: monocular RGB images and videos (§ 3.1 ), or other sensors (e.g., inertial measurement unit sensors, § 3.2 ). The majority of these methods use monocular RGB images and videos, and they are further divided into single-view single-person (§ 3.1.1 ); single-view multi-person (§ 3.1.2 ); and multi-view methods (§ 3.1.3 ).

records.subject: 2D HPE methods

claims.claim: 2D HPE methods estimate the 2D position or spatial location of human body keypoints from images or videos.

Deep learning-based approaches have achieved a major breakthrough in HPE by improving the results significantly.

records.quote: 2D HPE methods estimate the 2D position or spatial location of human body keypoints from images or videos. Recently, deep learning-based approaches have achieved a major breakthrough in HPE by improving the results significantly.

records.subject: Action samples of different data modalities

claims.claim: RGB modality provides rich appearance information, is easy to obtain and operate, and has a wide range of applications, but is sensitive to viewpoint, background, and illumination.

Skeleton modality provides 3D structural information of subject pose, is simple yet informative, and insensitive to viewpoint and background, but lacks appearance and detailed shape information and is noisy.
Depth modality provides 3D structural and geometric shape information, but lacks color and texture information and has limited workable distance.
Infrared Sequence modality is workable in dark environments, but lacks color and texture information and is susceptible to sunlight.
Point Cloud modality provides 3D information and geometric shape information, and is insensitive to viewpoint, but lacks color and texture information and has high computational complexity.

Event Stream modality avoids much visual redundancy, has high dynamic range, and no motion blur, but has asynchronous output, is spatio-temporally sparse, and the capturing device is relatively expensive.
Audio modality is easy to locate actions in temporal sequence, but lacks appearance information.
Acceleration modality can be used for fine-grained HAR, is privacy protecting, and low cost, but lacks appearance information and the capturing device needs to be carried by subject.

Radar modality can be used for through-wall HAR, is insensitive to illumination and weather, and is privacy protecting, but lacks appearance information and the capturing device is relatively expensive.
WiFi modality is simple and convenient, privacy protecting, and low cost, but lacks appearance information, is sensitive to environments, and is noisy.

records.subject: RGB video-based HAR methods

claims.claim: RGB video-based HAR methods can be mainly divided into four categories: two-stream 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), 3D CNN, and Transformer-based methods.

records.quote: we review, in the following, the advanced deep learning works for RGB-based HAR, which can be mainly divided into four categories, namely, two-stream 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), 3D CNN, and Transformer-based methods

records.claim: Zong et al. extended the two-stream CNN to a three-stream CNN by adding the motion saliency stream.
records.quote: Zong et al. [ 54 ] extended the two-stream CNN in [ 53 ] to a three-stream CNN by adding the motion saliency stream to better capture the salient motion information.

records.claim: The two-stream network was extended to a two-stream Siamese network to extract features from precondition and effect frames.
records.quote: Besides, the two-stream network has also been extended to a two-stream Siamese network to extract features from the frames before an action happens (precondition) and the frames after the action (effect)

records.subject: two-stream 2D CNN architectures

claims.claim: These architectures enable traditional 2D CNNs to effectively handle video data and achieve high HAR accuracy.
This type of architectures is still not powerful enough for long-term dependency modeling and has limitations in effectively modeling video-level temporal information.

records.quote: The two-stream 2D CNN architectures, that learn different types of information (e.g., spatial and temporal) from the input videos through separate networks and then perform fusion to get the final result, enable the traditional 2D CNNs to effectively handle the video data and achieve high HAR accuracy. However, this type of architectures is still not powerful enough for long-term dependency modeling, i.e., it has limitations in effectively modeling the video-level temporal information

records.claim: Gated RNN architectures are adopted to address the vanishing gradient problem of vanilla RNNs for modeling long-term temporal dependency.
records.quote: the traditional vanilla RNN suffers from the vanishing gradient problem... Thus, most of the existing methods have adopted gated RNN architectures

records.claim: RNN-based methods usually employ 2D CNNs as feature extractors followed by an LSTM model for HAR.
records.quote: RNN-based methods usually employ 2D CNNs, which serve as feature extractors, followed by an LSTM model for HAR.

records.claim: LRCN consists of a 2D CNN to extract frame-level RGB features followed by LSTMs to generate a single action label.
records.quote: Donahue et al. [ 7 ] introduced the Long-term Recurrent Convolutional Network (LRCN), which consists of a 2D CNN to extract frame-level RGB features followed by LSTMs

records.claim: Frame-level RGB and flow image features from pre-trained 2D CNNs are fed to a stacked LSTM framework for HAR.
records.quote: Ng et al. [ 71 ] extracted frame-level RGB and “flow image” features from pre-trained 2D CNNs, and then fed these features to a stacked LSTM framework

records.claim: An encoder LSTM maps input video to a fixed-length representation, which is decoded through a decoder LSTM for video reconstruction and prediction.
records.quote: an encoder LSTM was used to map an input video into a fixed-length representation, which was then decoded through a decoder LSTM

records.quote: Wu et al. [ 73 ] leveraged two LSTMs, which operate on coarse-scale and fine-scale CNN features cooperatively for efficient HAR.

records.subject: multi-modality fusion schemes in HAR

claims.claim: There are two widely used multi-modality fusion schemes in HAR, namely, score fusion and feature fusion.
score fusion integrates the decisions that are separately made based on different modalities to produce the final classification results.
feature fusion generally combines the features from different modalities to yield aggregated features that are often very discriminative and powerful for HAR.
data fusion, i.e., fusing the multi-modality input data before feature extraction, has also been exploited.
data fusion approaches are categorized under feature fusion.
claims.conditions: Since the input data can be treated as the original raw features

records.quote: There are two widely used multi-modality fusion schemes in HAR, namely, score fusion and feature fusion. Generally, the score fusion [ 362 ] integrates the decisions that are separately made based on different modalities (e.g., by weighted averaging [ 382 ] or by learning a score fusion model [ 361 ] ) to produce the final classification results. On the other hand, the feature fusion [ 379 ] generally combines the features from different modalities to yield aggregated features that are often very discriminative and powerful for HAR. Note that data fusion, i.e., fusing the multi-modality input data before feature extraction [ 404 ] , has also been exploited. Since the input data can be treated as the original raw features, here we simply categorize the data fusion approaches under feature fusion.

claims.claim: Early methods focused on extracting hand-crafted features which capture spatio-temporal structural relationships from the RGB and depth modalities for more reliable HAR.

Scene flow features were extracted from spatially aligned and temporally synchronized RGB and depth frames, utilizing bidirectional rank pooling to generate dynamic images fed to two different CNNs.

RGB and depth data were represented as two pairs of dynamic images passed through a cooperatively trained CNN (c-ConvNet) consisting of two streams exploiting features by jointly optimizing a ranking loss and a softmax loss.
A hybrid network consisting of multi-stream CNNs and 3D ConvLSTMs was introduced to extract features from RGB and depth videos, fused via canonical correlation analysis.

A generative framework was proposed to explore feature distribution across RGB and depth modalities, performing fusion by constructing a cross-modality discovery matrix fed to a modality correlation discovery network.

A two-stream network composed of a motion stream and a Shape Temporal Dynamic (STD) stream was designed to encode features from RGB and depth videos, with final scores obtained by aggregating the two streams.

A decoupling and recoupling spatio-temporal representation approach was proposed, using decoupled spatial and temporal networks and a self-distillation-based re-coupling spatio-temporal network with cross-modal adaptive posterior fusion.
claims.claims_about: decoupling and recoupling spatio-temporal representation approach

claims.claim: A Transformer framework for egocentric HAR was introduced where RGB and depth data are processed by an inter-frame attention encoder and fused by a mutual attention block.

records.quote: Early methods [ 411 , 412 ] focused on extracting hand-crafted features which capture spatio-temporal structural relationships from the RGB and depth modalities for more reliable HAR. In [ 359 ] , a four-stream deep CNN was introduced to extract features from different representations of depth data (i.e., three Depth Motion Maps [ 267 ] from three different viewpoints) and RGB data (i.e., a Motion History Image [ 413] ). The output scores of these four streams were fused to perform action classification. By considering the depth and RGB modalities as a single entity, Wang et al. [ 360 ] extracted scene flow features from the spatially aligned and temporally synchronized RGB and depth frames. The bidirectional rank pooling [ 55 ] was utilized to generate two dynamic images from the sequence of scene flow features. The dynamic images were then fed to two different CNNs, and finally, their classification scores were fused to perform HAR. Wang et al. [ 58 ] represented the RGB and depth data as two pairs of RGB and depth dynamic images, which were then passed through a cooperatively trained CNN (c-ConvNet). The c-ConvNet consists of two streams that exploit features for action classification by jointly optimizing a ranking loss and a softmax loss. In [ 363 ] , a hybrid network that consists of multi-stream CNNs and 3D ConvLSTMs [ 414 ] was introduced to extract features from RGB and depth videos. These features were then fused via canonical correlation analysis to perform action classification. Wang et al. [ 361 ] proposed a generative framework to explore the feature distribution across the RGB and depth modalities. The fusion was performed by constructing a cross-modality discovery matrix, which was then fed to a modality correlation discovery network for the final prediction. Dhiman et al. [ 362 ] designed a two-stream network composed of a motion stream and a Shape Temporal Dynamic (STD) stream to encode features from RGB and depth videos, respectively. Particularly, the motion stream takes a dynamic image from the RGB data as input and outputs classification scores. The STD network consists of the Human Pose Model in [ 9 ] as its backbone, followed by several LSTMs and a softmax layer. The final classification scores were obtained by aggregating the scores of these two streams. Transformers have also become popular for multi-modal fusion [ 364 , 366 ] . To handle the problem of tightly coupled spatio-temporal representation modeling, Zhou et al. [ 366 ] proposed a decoupling and recoupling spatio-temporal representation approach, which disentangles learning spatio-temporal representations. Specifically, decoupled spatial and temporal networks are introduced to learn spatial and temporal independent discriminative features, respectively. A self-distillation-based re-coupling spatio-temporal network consisting of a multi-scale layer and Transformer blocks is then employed to model spatio-temporal dependencies. Finally, a cross-modal adaptive posterior fusion method is utilized to perform information aggregation. Li et al. [ 364 ] introduced a Transformer framework for egocentric HAR, where RGB and its corresponding depth data are processed by an inter-frame attention encoder and then fused by a mutual attention block.

A pose guided spatio-temporal attention network was introduced on top of a 3D CNN model taking RGB videos as input.
A two-stream network consisting of an ST-GCN network, an R(2+1)D network, and a guided block was proposed, utilizing score fusion for classification.
A two-stream GCN network was introduced taking skeleton data and joint-aligned flow patches obtained from RGB videos as inputs.
Skeleton data was represented as a 3D heatmap volume and passed with the RGB video through a two-stream 3D CNN framework inspired by [ 112 ].

A Two-Pathway Vision Transformer (TP-ViT) was proposed to fuse RGB and skeleton data, consisting of a high-resolution path focusing on spatial information and a high-framerate path emphasizing temporal information.

records.quote: Zhao et al. [ 369 ] introduced a two-stream deep network, which consists of an RNN and a CNN to process skeleton and RGB data, respectively. Both the feature fusion and the score fusion were evaluated and the former achieved better performance. The two-stream architecture was also investigated in [ 368 , 370 ] , where the classification scores from a CNN model [ 370 ] or an RNN model [ 368 ] trained on skeleton data and a skeleton conditioned spatio-temporal attention network trained on RGB data were fused for final classification. Zolfaghari [ 367 ] designed a three-stream 3D-CNN to process pose, motion, and the raw RGB images. The three streams were fused via a Markov chain model for action classification. Liu et al. [ 8 ] proposed a spatio-temporal LSTM network, which is able to effectively fuse the RGB and skeleton features within the LSTM unit. In order to effectively capture the subtle variations in action performing, Song et al. [ 371 ] proposed a learning framework containing two streams of skeleton-guided deep CNN to extract features from RGB and optical flow. Particularly, the local image patches around human body parts were first extracted from both RGB and flow sequences, and then fed into two individual CNNs followed by a part-aggregated pooling layer to generate two fixed-length feature vectors corresponding to RGB and flow frames. The skeleton data and the two sequences of RGB and flow feature vectors were then passed through a three-stream LSTM model followed by a fusion layer to obtain the final classification scores. Das et al. [ 372 ] introduced a pose guided spatio-temporal attention network on top of a 3D CNN model taking RGB videos as input to perform HAR. In their subsequent work [ 374 ] , they extended their work in [ 372 ] by paying attention to the topology of the human body while computing the spatio-temporal attention maps. Li et al. [ 373 ] proposed a two-stream network, which consists of three main components namely the ST-GCN network [ 186 ] to extract the skeleton features, R(2+1)D network [ 109 ] to extract RGB features, and a guided block which takes these features to enhance the action-related information in RGB videos. Finally, the score fusion approach was utilized to perform classification. Cai et al. [ 376 ] introduced a two-stream GCN network, respectively taking skeleton data and joint-aligned flow patches obtained from RGB videos as the inputs for HAR. RGBPose-Conv3D [ 378 ] represents skeleton data as a 3D heatmap volume and passes the RGB video and the heatmap volume through a two-stream 3D CNN framework whose architecture is inspired by [ 112 ] . Recently, Jing and Wang [ 377 ] proposed a Two-Pathway Vision Transformer (TP-ViT) to fuse RGB and skeleton data, which consists of a high-resolution path focusing on spatial information and a high-framerate path emphasizing the temporal information.

records.quote: Continual learning in the literature is also referred to as: lifelong learning ( Silver and Mercer, 2002 ; Silver et al., 2013 ; Chen and Liu, 2018 ; Chaudhry et al., 2019a ; Parisi et al., 2019 ; Aljundi et al., 2017 ) , incremental learning ( Solomonoff, 1989 ; Chaudhry et al., 2018 ) , sequential learning ( McCloskey and Cohen, 1989 ; Shin et al., 2017 ; Aljundi et al., 2019 ) , explanation-based learning ( Thrun, 1996 ) , and never-ending learning ( Carlson et al., 2010 ) .

records.subject: Transfer learning

claims.claim: Transferring knowledge from a source task/domain to a target task/domain to improve the performance of the target task.
Aligned with forward transfer; unaligned with backward transfer, knowledge retention, task boundaries, and off-line learning.
claims.conditions: Properties aligned (+) and unaligned (–) with CL

records.quote: Transfer learning | Transferring knowledge from a source task/domain to a target task/domain to improve the performance of the target task. | + forward transfer – no backward transfer – no knowledge retention – task boundaries – off-line learning | ( Pan and Yang, 2010 ) ( Howard and Ruder, 2018 ) ( Peters et al., 2018 ) ( Radford et al., 2019 ) ( Devlin et al., 2019 ) ( Houlsby et al., 2019 ) ( Raffel et al., 2020 )

records.subject: Multi-task learning

claims.claim: Learning multiple related tasks jointly, using parameter sharing, to improve the generalization of all the tasks.

claims.conditions: Properties aligned (+) and unaligned (–) with CL

records.quote: Multi-task learning | Learning multiple related tasks jointly, using parameter sharing, to improve the generalization of all the tasks. | + positive transfer – negative transfer – task boundaries – off-line learning | ( Caruana, 1997 ) ( Zhang and Yang, 2017 ) ( Ruder, 2017 ) ( McCann et al., 2018 ) ( Stickland and Murray, 2019 ) ( Phang et al., 2020 )

records.subject: Meta-learning

claims.claim: Learning to learn. Learning generic knowledge, given a small set of training examples and numerous tasks, and quickly adapting to a new task.
Aligned with forward transfer; unaligned with backward transfer, knowledge retention, and off-line learning.
claims.conditions: Properties aligned (+) and unaligned (–) with CL

records.quote: Meta-learning | Learning to learn. Learning generic knowledge, given a small set of training examples and numerous tasks, and quickly adapting to a new task. | + forward transfer – no backward transfer – no knowledge retention – off-line learning | ( Thrun and Pratt, 1998 ) ( Finn et al., 2017 ) ( Xu et al., 2018 ) ( Obamuyide and Vlachos, 2019 ) ( Hospedales et al., 2020 ) ( Beaulieu et al., 2020 )

records.subject: Curriculum learning

claims.claim: Learning from training examples arranged in a meaningful order – task or data difficulty gradually increases.
Aligned with forward transfer, backward transfer, and knowledge retention; unaligned with task boundaries and off-line learning.
claims.conditions: Properties aligned (+) and unaligned (–) with CL

records.quote: Curriculum learning | Learning from training examples arranged in a meaningful order – task or data difficulty gradually increases. | + forward transfer + backward transfer + knowledge retention – task boundaries – off-line learning | ( Elman, 1993 ) ( Bengio et al., 2009 ) ( van der Wees et al., 2017 ) ( Zhang et al., 2018 ) ( Zhang et al., 2019 ) ( Platanios et al., 2019 ) ( Ruiter et al., 2020 )

records.subject: On-line learning

claims.claim: Learning over a continuous stream of training examples provided in a sequential order. Experiences concept drift due to non-i.i.d. data.
Aligned with on-line learning and forward transfer; unaligned with backward transfer, knowledge retention, and single task/domain.
claims.conditions: Properties aligned (+) and unaligned (–) with CL

records.quote: On-line learning | Learning over a continuous stream of training examples provided in a sequential order. Experiences concept drift due to non-i.i.d. data. | + on-line learning + forward transfer – no backward transfer – no knowledge retention – single task/domain | ( Bottou, 1999 ) ( Bottou and LeCun, 2004 ) ( Cesa-Bianchi and Lugosi, 2006 ) ( Shalev-Shwartz, 2012 ) ( C. de Souza et al., 2015 ) ( Hoi et al., 2018 )

records.subject: On-the-job learning

claims.claim: Discovering new tasks, learning and adapting on-the-fly. On-the-job learning operates in an open-world environment, and it involves interaction with humans and the environment. It belongs to the CL family of methods.
Aligned with on-line learning, forward transfer, backward transfer, knowledge retention, no task boundaries, and open-world learning; unaligned with interactive learning.
claims.conditions: Properties aligned (+) and unaligned (–) with CL

records.subject: NLP benchmark datasets

claims.claim: XCOPA is a typologically diverse multilingual dataset for causal commonsense reasoning covering 11 languages from distinct families.
WebText is a dataset of millions of webpages suitable for learning language models without supervision, containing 45 million links scraped from Reddit and 40 GB of data.
C4 is a dataset constructed from Common Crawl’s web crawl corpus serving as a source of unlabeled text data, with a size of 17 GB.
Lifelong FewRel consists of sentence-relation pairs derived from Wikipedia distributed over 10 disjoint clusters representing different tasks.
Lifelong Simple Questions consists of single-relation questions divided into 20 disjoint clusters resulting in 20 tasks.

records.subject: hardware-aware neural architecture search

claims.claim: There exist mainly three types of heuristic search algorithms: evolutionary algorithms, reinforcement learning, and differentiable NAS.

records.quote: In the literature, there exist mainly three types of heuristic search algorithms for the hardware-aware neural architecture search, which are (1) evolutionary algorithms, (2) reinforcement learning, and (3) differentiable NAS.

records.claim: ProxylessNAS can reduce the computational demand of the search by executing partial tasks.
records.quote: The ProxylessNAS [ 151 ] can reduce the computational demand of the search by executing partial tasks, such as training on a smaller dataset, or learning with only a few blocks, or training just for a few epochs.

records.claim: MnasNet directly implements and measures the inference latency by executing the model on mobile phones.
records.quote: The MnasNet approach [ 152 ] directly implements and measures the inference latency by executing the model on mobile phones, and incorporates the model latency into the main objective of the search, along with the accuracy.

records.claim: NASCaps is a framework integrating capsule layers in the search space using a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm.
records.quote: The NASCaps [ 154 ] is a framework integrating capsule layers in the search space. With a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm, it jointly optimizes the accuracy and the hardware efficiency of capsule-based DNNs.

records.claim: APNAS is a reinforcement learning-based exploration methodology that estimates cycle count by analytical models to speed-up the search.
records.quote: The APNAS [ 156 ] is a reinforcement learning-based exploration methodology, searching for high accurate DNNs that also offer high execution performance. To speed-up the search, instead of running millions of DNN configurations on real hardware, the cycle count is estimated by analytical models.

records.claim: FNAS performs a hardware-aware NAS targeting FPGA acceleration and employs an abstraction model to estimate the latency.
records.quote: The FNAS framework [ 157 ] performs a hardware-aware NAS targeting FPGA acceleration. In particular, it employs an abstraction model to estimate the latency for meeting the specifications.

records.claim: HotNAS is a hardware and neural architecture co-search methodology which starts the exploration from a set of existing pre-trained models.
records.quote: The HotNAS [ 158 ] is a hardware and neural architecture co-search methodology, which starts the exploration from a set of existing pre-trained models to reduce the training time.

records.claim: With the ENAS approach, the authors proposed to share the parameters between the child DNN models to speedup the search.
records.quote: With the ENAS approach [ 159 ] , the authors proposed to share the parameters between the child DNN models. It allows not only to speedup the search, but also to achieve high accuracy, with similar benefits as for the transfer learning [ 160 ] .

records.claim: Single-Path NAS is a method searching for the optimal building block for the convolutional layers, called superkernel.
records.quote: The Single-Path NAS [ 161 ] is a method searching for the optimal building block for the convolutional layers, called superkernel, and then sharing the convolutional kernel weights with a specialized encoding.

records.claim: DNAS is a differentiable NAS framework where the search space is represented by a stochastic super net.
records.quote: The DNAS [ 162 ] is a differentiable NAS framework, where the search space is represented by a stochastic super net. It explores a layer-wise space where each layer of the CNN can choose a different block, and the learning process is done by training the stochastic super net.

records.claim: SPOS uses in a similar way the supernet concept to perform NAS, where constraints such as latency and number of FLOPs are applied.
records.quote: The SPOS [ 163 ] uses in a similar way the supernet concept to perform NAS, where the constraints such as latency and number of FLOPs are applied.

records.claim: The HURRICANE framework performs a two-stage search algorithm for the automatic hardware-aware NAS.
records.quote: The HURRICANE framework [ 164 ] performs a two-stage search algorithm for the automatic hardware-aware NAS. It can generate different models for different types of hardware platforms for executing the inference.

records.quote: With the Ristretto framework, complex models such as AlexNet [ 40 ] , SqueezeNet [ 174 ] or GoogleNet [ 43 ] are inferred on 8 bits with less than 1% accuracy loss.

records.subject: variable-bitwidth HW platforms

claims.claim: BISMO supports variable precision from 1 to 8 bits using bit-serial computation.
Stripes uses bit-serial operations with flexible bitwidth for activations.
UNPU keeps activation bits constant at 16-bits while weights have variable bitwidth.
Loom adopts bit-serial multiplicators with fully variable bitwidth (1-16 bit) for both weights and activations.
Bit Fusion implements variable precision operations using a spatial approach with an array of bit-level PEs.
Turing TC supports operations from 32/16-bit floating-point down to 8/4-bit fixed-point.
PowerVR S2NX has adjustable bitwidth from 16 to 4 bits.

records.quote: The metrics in this family evaluate disentanglement by fixing factors and creating subsets of data points. Codes and factors in the subsets are compared to produce a score. records.subject: Conventinal learning-based methods

claims.claim: Hand-crafted features include intensity features, intensity gradient features, bifurcation feature vectors, spatial location, and angles.

Statistical models include Threshold, Intensity/appearance model, and Topological model.

records.section: 2 Vessel tracking using conventional machine learning

records.claim: Zhang et al. (2017b) used vascular filters to extract features and integrated them into a structured random forest for voxel classification.
records.quote: Using vascular filters (e.g., Frangi filter and optimally oriented flux), Zhang et al. (2017b) extracted the corresponding types of vascular features and integrated these feature responses into a structured random forest to classify voxels into positive and negative classes.

records.claim: Annunziata and Trucco (2016) proposed a warm-start strategy based on hand-crafted filters which are then refined by convolutional sparse coding.
records.quote: This strategy is based on carefully designing hand-crafted filters and modeling appearance properties of curvilinear structures, which are then refined by convolutional sparse coding.

records.claim: Sironi et al. (2015) accelerated the learning process by computing filters via linear combination with a smaller number of separable filters.
records.quote: To accelerate the learning process, Sironi et al. (2015) computed the filters by linearly combining them with a smaller number of separable filters.

records.claim: Annunziata et al. (2015a) introduced context information into the filter-learning process in addition to appearance features.
records.quote: In addition to the appearance features of learning filters, Annunziata et al. (2015a) introduced the context information (i.e., relationships among objects) in the filter-learning process.

records.subject: hand-crafted features

claims.claim: Conventional machine-learning-based methods train models with numerous hand-crafted features which should be well-designed according to the applications.
These features can be obtained by a series of filters.

records.quote: Conventional machine-learning-based methods train models with numerous hand-crafted features, which should be well-designed according to the applications. These features (i.e., global and local features) can be obtained by a series of filters

records.claim: Kande et al. (2010) used a thresholding technique based on the spatially weighted fuzzy C-means algorithm to preserve spatial structures.
records.quote: Kande et al. (2010) used a thresholding technique based on the spatially weighted fuzzy C-means algorithm, which can well preserve the spatial structures in a binarized/thresholded image.

records.claim: Zeng et al. (2018) constructed the intensity model based on kernel fuzzy C-means to extract the intensity feature of thick vessels.
records.quote: Zeng et al. (2018) constructed the intensity model based on kernel fuzzy C-means to extract the intensity feature of thick vessels.

records.claim: AdaBoost is described as a special case of boosting-based methods trained to detect bifurcation points.
records.quote: As a special case of boosting-based methods, the AdaBoost learning model is trained to automatically detect the bifurcation points of vessels with elaborately selected features.

records.claim: The PBT classifier is defined as a classification tree with an AdaBoost classifier at each node.
records.quote: If a classification tree has an AdaBoost classifier at each node, then the tree will be the probabilistic boosting-tree (PBT) classifier.

records.subject: classification methodologies

claims.claim: Methodologies of classification are broadly categorized into unsupervised and supervised learning strategies.

records.quote: For vessel-tracking tasks, the methodologies of classification can be broadly categorized into the unsupervised and supervised learning strategies.

records.subject: supervised learning methods

claims.claim: Most supervised methods use SVM, boosting-based methods, and random forests to distinguish vascular patterns.

records.quote: Most of these methods in the supervised category use various classifiers (Fig. 2 )—support vector machine (SVM), boosting-based methods, and random forests—to distinguish the vascular patterns in the images.

records.claim: Rani et al. (2016) combined the SVM and tree-bagger techniques to distinguish between the vessel and non-vessel structures.
records.quote: Rani et al. (2016) combined the SVM and tree-bagger techniques to distinguish between the vessel and non-vessel structures.

records.claim: The works of Lugauer et al. (2014) and Chapman et al. (2015) used the RF, PBT, and logistic regression classifier to identify the lumen contours and edges of vessels.
records.quote: The works of Lugauer et al. (2014) and Chapman et al. (2015) used the RF, PBT, and logistic regression classifier to identify the lumen contours and edges of vessels.

records.claim: Hu et al. (2018b) intricately applied the cascade-AdaBoost-SVM classifiers to delineate the vessel boundaries.
records.quote: Hu et al. (2018b) intricately applied the cascade-AdaBoost-SVM classifiers to delineate the vessel boundaries.

records.subject: techniques in deep-learning-based methods

claims.claim: CNN + Dilated convolution technique is associated with Wolterink et al. (2019), Mou et al. (2019), and Nazir et al. (2020).
CNN + Deformation convolution technique is associated with Jin et al. (2019).
CNN + No Pooling technique is associated with Liskowski and Krawiec (2016) and Tetteh et al. (2017).

records.subject: neural networks interpretability approaches

claims.claim: There exists three main approaches to interpret neural networks categorized by accessibility: Self-interpretable System, Representation Analysis, and Re-approximation.

records.quote: There exists three main approaches to interpret neural networks. We categorize these three main branches by how much accessibility and permission a method needs to have to interpret a neural network model: requiring full access and modification ( Self-interpretable System ), requiring full access without modification ( Representation Analysis ), or requiring no access or modification privilege ( Re-approximation )

records.subject: Self-Interpretable System

records.quote: Self-Interpretable System is a method that designs a neural network in a way that it can somewhat explain its decision. This approach requires to fully access the model to be able to modify and architect the neural network.

records.subject: Representation Analysis

claims.claim: Deep neural networks are internally divided by smaller subcomponents: layers, individual neurons, vectors, and input information.
ResNet50 is organized into 50 layers, with each layer computing between 64 to 2048 neurons, and the final layer contains a vector of 2048 dimensions.

records.quote: deep neural networks are internally divided by smaller subcomponents. The subcomponents are layers individual neurons , vectors , and input information . For example, ResNet50 can be organized into 50 layers, and each layer computes between 64 to 2048 neurons. The final layer of ResNet50 contains a vector of 2048 dimensions.

records.subject: Re-approximation

claims.claim: Re-approximation uses interpretable models to understand neural networks by monitoring input and output without reading or modifying the model.

records.quote: Re-approximation uses genuinely interpretable models to understand the neural networks. This approach does not read or modify the model to understand it. It simply monitors input and output of the model and re-approximates for interpretation.

records.subject: CML approaches

claims.claim: CML approaches are categorized into pure software-based cryptographic protocols, perturbation-based approaches, and hardware-assisted approaches.
Cryptographic protocols are divided into homogeneous approaches using one primitive and hybrid approaches using multiple primitives.
Perturbation-based approaches depend on data transformations and secret parameters, offering weaker security but higher efficiency.
Hardware-assisted approaches depend on trusted execution environments like Intel SGX to enforce secure enclaves.

records.quote: We focus on the major category of methods: the pure software-based cryptographic protocols , while also briefly reviewing the perturbation-based approaches and the hardware-assisted approaches.

records.subject: CML development strategies

claims.claim: Researchers often use the Decomposition-Mapping-Composition (DMC) procedure to transform machine learning algorithms for CML.
A unique feature of CML development is finding 'crypto-friendly' alternative machine learning algorithms or components.

records.quote: To make the transformation easier, researchers often implicitly use the Decomposition-Mapping-Composition (DMC) procedure: decomposing the target algorithm into different subcomponents, mapping the sub-components to crypto-primitives, and composing the CML framework with the confidential sub-components.

records.subject: Homogeneous Cryptographic Approaches

claims.claim: Homogeneous approaches rely on a single primitive to construct the framework protocols.

The primitives used in the homogeneous composition of CML are broadly in two categories: (1) Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) and Garbled Circuits (GC) and (2) Additively Homomorphic Encryption (AHE) and Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption (SHE).
FHE and GC are, therefore, the most expressive privacy primitives.

records.quote: Homogeneous approaches rely on a single primitive to construct the framework protocols. The primitives used in the homogeneous composition of CML are broadly in two categories: (1) Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) and Garbled Circuits (GC) and (2) Additively Homomorphic Encryption (AHE) and Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption (SHE). Since FHE implements arbitrary levels of homomorphic addition and multiplication and GC implements the boolean gates, in theory, they can individually construct all CML algorithms. FHE and GC are, therefore, the most expressive privacy primitives. However, both FHE and GC are too expensive to be practical when mapped to for training complex CML models. Oppositely, AHE and SHE schemes provide limited support for encrypted operations, therefore, less expressive and can only enable relatively simple algorithms.

records.subject: Empirical Cost Comparison

claims.claim: AHE scheme has the most efficient arithmetic additions and multiplications.
2-party garbled circuits are the only viable option for comparison and division.
Vectorized additions and multiplications are much more efficient than non-vectorized ones due to message packing in RLWE.
RLWE with message packing realizes homomorphic additions more efficiently when compared to the Paillier scheme.
RLWE scheme with vectorized linear algebraic operation is still slower than the Paillier solutions.
Randomized secret sharing is almost free for vector addition but involves higher computation and communication costs for dot product and matrix-vector multiplication.
Garbled circuits appear to be the worst solution for the confidential versions of the linear algebraic operation with higher computation and communication costs between the two parties.
Paillier implementation shows performance advantages over RLWE on arithmetic operations, but requires one operand to be plaintext.
Paillier’s encryption and decryption costs are higher than that of RLWE.

records.quote: We have observed that the AHE scheme has the most efficient arithmetic additions and multiplications. However, for comparison and division, the 2-party garbled circuits are the only viable option. ... The RLWE with message packing realizes homomorphic additions more efficiently when compared to the Paillier scheme. ... the RLWE scheme with the vectorized linear algebraic operation is still slower than the Paillier solutions. Randomized secret sharing is almost free for vector addition but involves higher computation and communication costs for the dot product and matrix-vector multiplication. Garbled circuits appear to be the worst solution for the confidential versions of the linear algebraic operation with higher computation and communication costs between the two parties. Although the Paillier implementation shows performance advantages over RLWE on arithmetic operations, it requires one operand to be plaintext. Paillier’s encryption and decryption costs, however, are higher than that of RLWE [ 12 ] .

records.subject: Mapping Taxonomy with DELC stages and Attack Vectors

claims.claim: In the Delivery stage, Phishing attacks are primarily detected using Context Inspection (24 studies) and Direct Inspection (12 studies).

In the Exploitation stage, Malware/RAT attacks are primarily detected using Event-based Approach (4 studies), Flow-based Approach (1 study), Hybrid Approach (1 study), and Propagation based Approach (1 study).

In the Command Control stage, Overt Channels are primarily detected using Flow-based Approach (6 studies), Hybrid Approach (2 studies), Context Inspection (1 study), and Event-based Approach (1 study).
In the Concealment stage, Data Tunneling is primarily detected using Flow-based Approach (7 studies), Distribution Inspection (3 studies), and Context Inspection (2 studies).

In the Multi-Stage stage, Insider Attack is primarily detected using Event-based Approach (8 studies), Distribution Inspection (1 study), Hybrid Approach (1 study), and Resource usage -based Approach (1 study).

records.subject: Feature Selection Methods

claims.claim: Filter methods are computationally fast, simple to implement, and classifier independent, but have low performance and require manual threshold setting.
Wrapper methods offer good performance for specific models and consider feature dependencies, but are classifier dependent and computationally expensive.

Embedded methods learn good features in parallel to decision boundary learning and are less expensive than wrappers, but require fine-grain understanding of classifier implementation and are computationally expensive than filters.
Dimension Reduction techniques are computationally fast, transform features to low dimension, and are classifier independent, but are not interpretable and require manual threshold setting.
Attention mechanisms decrease development time of DL methods, automatically learn relevant features without manual thresholds, and yield significant performance gain, but are not reliable.

records.quote: Methods | Description | Strengths | Weaknesses | Filter [ 79 ] | These approaches select the best features by analyzing the statistical relationship between features and their label. Popular filter methods include information gain, correlation analysis and Chi-square test. | • Computational fast speed [ 79 ] , • Ignore classifier biases and heuristics. • Simple to implement and comprehend • classifier independent | • Low performance [ 28 ] as not classifier dependent • Requires manually setting the thresholds. | Wrapper [ 80 ] | These approaches consider the classifier used for classification to select the best features. Popular wrapper method includes genetic algorithm and sequential search. | • Good performance for specific model. • Consider features dependencies | • Classifier dependent • Computationally expensive | Embedded [ 79 ] | These techniques use both advantages of filter and wrapper method to select the best features. Popular embedded methods include Random Forest Trees, XG-Boost, Ada-boost. | • Learn good features in parallel to learning the decision boundary. • Less expensive than wrappers. | • Need for fine-grain understanding of classifier implementation • Computationally expensive than filter. • Classifier specific | Dimension Reduction [ 81 ] | These techniques select the optimal feature set to decrease the dimensions of the feature vector. Popular methods include PCA, LDA and Iso-maps. | • Computational fast speed [ 79 ] • Transform features to low dimension. • Classifier independent. | • Not interpretable. • Manually setting for threshold is required. | Attention [ 82 ] | In 2017 a mechanism for Deep Learning (DL) approaches that focus on certain factors than other when processing data [ 85 ] . | • Decrease development time of DL methods. • Automatically learns relevant features without manual thresholds. • Yield a significant performance gain [ 86 ] . | • Not reliable [ 83 , 84 ] .

records.subject: RF based localization methods

claims.claim: RF based localization methods can be roughly categorised into four main classes: Trilateration and triangulation methods, Proximity, Fingerprint matching, and Direct methods.

records.quote: RF based localization methods can be roughly categorised into four main classes: • Trilateration and triangulation methods . • Proximity . • Fingerprint matching . • Direct methods .

records.subject: Trilateration and triangulation methods

claims.claim: The system uses one or more observed quantities to infer the distance or the angles between the target and anchors, then applies simple geometric calculation to infer the coordinates of the target.
GNSS, and, more generally, time-of-arrival (ToA) -based trilateration are the most important example of this category.

records.quote: The system uses one or more observed quantities to infer the distance or the angles between the target (i.e., a wireless node whose position we wish to determine), and anchors (i.e., nodes with known location). It then applies simple geometric calculation to infer the coordinates of the target. GNSS, and, more generally, time-of-arrival (ToA) -based trilateration [ 2 ] are the most important example of this category.

records.subject: Proximity

claims.claim: In these solutions, the goal is to identify whether a target is within a certain range from an infrastructure node (e.g., a sensing devices).

records.quote: In these solutions, the goal is to identify whether a target is within a certain range from an infrastructure node (e.g., a sensing devices).

records.subject: Fingerprint matching

claims.claim: The system relies on the availability of a database that contains the fingerprints, i.e., observations of characteristics of signals at a set of locations; when localization of a target is required, the system uses either statistical or deterministic methods to match the observed signal to one of the priori stored fingerprints to infer the approximate user coordinates.
The construction of the database is usually done ”offline”, e.g., when the system is initially deployed.

records.quote: In this type of solutions, the system relies on the availability of a database that contains the fingerprints, i.e., observations of characteristics of signals at a set of locations; when localization of a target is required, the system uses either statistical or deterministic methods to match the observed signal to one of the priori stored fingerprints to infer the approximate user coordinates. The construction of the database is usually done ”offline”, e.g., when the system is initially deployed.

records.subject: Direct methods

claims.claim: In these solutions, the system estimates the coordinates directly without estimating latent quantities such as distances and angles.
A possible way is through a set of assumptions about the joint relation between the coordinates and wireless channels, e.g., statistical models.

records.subject: ML-based localization solutions

claims.claim: ML-based localization solutions are differentiated into three types: Region classification, Fingerprint classification, and coordinates estimation.

records.quote: We here differentiate between three types: (i) Region classification, (ii) Fingerprint classification, (iii) and coordinates estimation.

records.subject: Region classification

claims.claim: Region classification aims to identify a sub-region (building, floor, or room) and can be interpreted as a classification problem with low misclassification error and possibly reduced computational effort.

records.quote: Region classification means that the system aims to identify a sub-region of the study area in which the target is located, such as the building, floor, or room. This can be interpreted as finding the location with a certain, more or less rough, quantization, or, in other words, a classification problem.

records.subject: Fingerprint localization

claims.claim: Fingerprint localization matches the target to the closest fingerprint (Reference Point) in the database and can be viewed as a classification problem with N distinguished classes.

records.quote: Alternatively, in fingerprint localization, the solution could be to match the target to the closest fingerprint in the database, also known as Reference Point (RP). Also this solution approach can be viewed as classification problem with N N distinguished classes, where N N is the number of RPs in the database.

records.subject: coordinates estimation

claims.claim: Coordinates estimation provides explicit coordinates of the target and can be seen as a regression problem in the context of ML.

records.quote: The most natural localization solution is to provide the explicit coordinates of the target; in the context of ML this can be seen as a regression problem.

records.subject: localization systems

claims.claim: Active localization involves targets equipped with wireless transceivers that participate in the process, allowing easy differentiation of different targets.
Passive localization involves targets without wireless transceivers that only reflect signals, often referred to as device-free localization or radar.
Semi-passive localization involves passive RFID tags that reflect signals in a unique way for a particular tag, allowing distinction of signals from different targets.

records.quote: Active localization : here the target is equipped with a wireless transceiver, and participates in the localization process. Due to the operating principle, different targets can be easily differentiated. ... Passive localization : here, the target does not have a wireless transceiver, but rather only reflects a signal; this is sometimes referred to as device-free localization, and more often as radar. ... Semi-passive localization : a borderline case are passive RFID tags. While they are passive in the sense that they do not contain transceivers and only reflect signals, they do so in a way that is unique for a particular tag, and thus allow distinction of the signals from different targets.

During the offline phase, the environment is surveyed at predefined locations (RPs) and certain features of the RF signal are recorded; location of the RPs and the recorded features at those points are then stored in a database (radio-map).
records.section: IV-F Features Utilization in Conventional and ML-based Localization Systems

records.claim: Straightforward linear searches are too computationally intensive for large databases; a hierarchical search is preferable for fast fingerprint matching.
records.conditions: in particular when large databases are available
records.quote: Straightforward linear searches are too computationally intensive in particular when large databases are available; rather a hierarchical search is preferable.
records.section: IV-F Features Utilization in Conventional and ML-based Localization Systems

records.claim: Used for tracking target trajectories by predicting location change based on previous movement and correcting estimates from new measurements, filtering out noise.
records.quote: Such tracking, or in general utilization of previous observations (historical data), is usually done by means of Kalman filters or particle filters [ 1 ] . They predict the change of location in a timestep based on the previous movement, and subsequently correct the estimate from measurements of the new location.
records.section: IV-F Features Utilization in Conventional and ML-based Localization Systems

records.claim: Used in fingerprinting solutions for feature extraction, radio-map construction, radio-map updating, hierarchical solutions, and robust matching.
records.quote: Since then it has been utilized in other aspects as well, for instance for feature extraction and radio-map construction [ 297 , 231 , 103 , 154 , 72 , 91 , 94 , 138 , 142 , 72 ] , radio-map updating [ 181 , 132 , 122 , 85 ] , hierarchical solutions [ 316 , 222 , 151 , 256 , 75 ] , and robust matching [ 79 , 88 , 86 ] .
records.section: IV-F Features Utilization in Conventional and ML-based Localization Systems

records.claim: Can be used as an end-to-end (direct) localization solution without the need for explicit radio-map construction.
records.quote: Nevertheless, ML-based solutions span a wider scope as, for instance, ML could be used as an end-to-end (i.e., direct) localization solution, without the need for an explicit radio-map construction
records.section: IV-F Features Utilization in Conventional and ML-based Localization Systems

records.claim: Advances in recurrent DL methods can potentially eliminate the need for restrictive assumptions about the location evolution process in tracking.
records.quote: the advances of recurrent DL methods can potentially eliminate the need for such restrictive assumptions.
